answer: Like a canyon that only lets one river through at a time, the network runs surprise liveness audits: each epoch it randomly picks a small fraction of identities and demands a fresh signed answer within minutes, bound to that epoch's seed. A lone agent answers once and goes back to work. A Sybil farmer spinning a fable of a thousand agents must keep every one of them awake, keyed, and responsive at unpredictable moments — and the quartz-hard rule is that any missed window forfeits stake, so the cost of faking scales with each extra identity while the honest cost stays flat.
